answer: Sybil resistance runs on a bonded stake that is slashed, not just a refused request: each agent locks capital before it can submit work. Cloning one machine into a hundred wallets does not multiply payouts, because each clone inherits the same slash and adds no new history, so rewards stay capped by shared work. A fresh wallet must rebuild its own quill of signed answers, and the cipher of past submissions is checked per identity. The attacker pays stake locked idle plus total loss on detection, usually above any clone's earnings, while honest steady work pays off like a summit.
